title: URL, URLSearchParams, and History
learningObjectives: Explain url, urlsearchparams, and history and use the browser API with appropriate lifecycle and privacy safeguards.

understand.concept: URL parses and edits URL components; URLSearchParams manages query parameters; the History API adds or replaces same-document navigation entries and reports back/forward changes through popstate. These APIs work together for shareable application state.
understand.whyItMatters: Structured URL APIs avoid fragile string concatenation. History changes should be reflected in the UI, and query parameters must not be treated as trusted authorization.
understand.analogy: URL is the address record, search parameters are its query fields, and History is the navigation trail.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser API support, permission, lifecycle, and security rules vary by platform.

explain.narrative: The current URL receives a query parameter and a history entry. The app must still render the matching view and handle popstate.

examples.explanation: The current URL receives a query parameter and a history entry. The app must still render the matching view and handle popstate.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console or UI output demonstrates the API; permission and secure-context features require a supported environment.

practise.guidedTask: Build a filterable course list whose selected filter is stored in the URL and restored on back/forward navigation.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using the API. Include feature detection, permission or failure handling, cleanup, and an accessible alternative where relevant.
hints: Do not assume the API is available in every browser.
Request sensitive permissions only after explaining why.
Clean up observers, workers, and listeners when no longer needed.

questions.prompt: Which event is fired when the active history entry changes through back or forward navigation?
questions.explanation: popstate notifies the page when the active same-document history entry changes.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach when using browser APIs?
options: Feature-detect, handle denial or failure, and clean up resources
questions.answer: Feature-detect, handle denial or failure, and clean up resources
questions.explanation: Browser features need graceful fallback, privacy-aware permission, and lifecycle management.
